weaknesses.quote: Defuse legacy risk once if the HR remark is not the friendly one
weaknesses.problem: The handbook publishes no statistical effect for Defuse legacy risk, yet the quarterly section presents it as the fixed first response to a warning. The rule is an untested assumption stated as a game mechanic.
weaknesses.fix: Label it as a working assumption, and tell the agent to check the next observe output for any stat change before relying on it again.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: Combined with step 2, this drops nearly every story option, so the agent falls back on the vague 'smallest and most reversible risk' rule. Outcomes then depend on how the agent reads 'doubt', which hurts consistency across event wordings.
weaknesses.fix: Add a concrete tie-breaker: if more than one option survives step 2, keep the one that most directly raises a stat not in Stalled. Only treat options as risky when a listed trigger in step 2 applies.

weaknesses.quote: **Near a limit.** Health or Dignity in the lower part of its 0–10 range
weaknesses.problem: The near-limit section omits two published failure directions: repeated low performance (C or D review grades) and Skill falling materially behind. It also has no rule for the trust crisis after a second blow-up, which the handbook names as a run-ending risk.
weaknesses.fix: Add a line: 'Two C or D review grades in a row, or Skill falling behind expectations: spend the next Energy on Skill learning or Prepare report materials and set the main action to Apply for a key project; after any second blow-up, drop all risk-raising options for the next two stories.'

weaknesses.quote: a provisional record of an expected gain that did not show up in this run
weaknesses.problem: The Stalled/Expect mechanism needs the agent to store expected values at one quarterly choice, compare them at the next, and carry the result across summaries. That is multi-step bookkeeping a model will often get wrong, and it adds little to the core decision.
weaknesses.fix: Replace it with one rule: after a quarterly action, compare each stat with its value before the action. If a stat rose less than the action's displayed change, do not repeat that action for it next quarter. Drop the Expect field and the Stalled list.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0
weaknesses.problem: The required note header packs five separate counters into one line, and several are defined only elsewhere (Best reset rules, Stalled, Concerns). The agent must recompute and copy all of them each turn, which invites errors and makes the note hard to parse when a summary cuts the run.
weaknesses.fix: Require only the fields that drive a decision: Review in N and the current Skill, Network and Output. Keep Best as a separate rule, and remove Stalled and Concerns from the mandatory header or cap them at a short, fixed list.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: The hidden-risk list is long and mostly the authors' guesses, and this default tells the agent to drop anything ambiguous. Combined with step 2, this can starve choices in every month and push the agent away from Output and Skill gains. It also conflicts with the N = 1 exception, which allows some risk at review time.
weaknesses.fix: Give a short, prioritised list of clearly risky behaviours (hiding, denying, blaming, gambling, side deals) and a default for ambiguous options when the HR remark is friendly. State the review-month exception once, in the same place.

weaknesses.quote: While a stat is in Stalled, prefer another useful investment over paying again for it.
weaknesses.problem: Stalled depends on Expect values the agent estimates from displayed changes, and on a note-based check that is lost after summaries. A wrong estimate can lock a stat out of investment for many quarters, which starves Skill, Network or Output.
weaknesses.fix: Only record a stall when the observed stat change is clearly absent after a displayed gain. Clear it after one quarter, and drop the Expect bookkeeping.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count, and a single lost point there can cost the promotion.
weaknesses.problem: This presents an invented timing rule as fact. The handbook only says a promotion window opens every six months and does not say when assessment or the review talk happens, so the N = 1 deadline and the Review close steps rest on an unverified mechanic.
weaknesses.fix: Label the timing as a working assumption, as the Story section does. Or base the deadline on the published window and tell the agent to read the review talk when it arrives.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: This conflicts with the step 2 exception that allows mild risk in the N = 1 month when the HR remark is friendly or quiet. The agent gets two incompatible thresholds for the same choice and no concrete test for what counts as mild.
weaknesses.fix: Pick one rule for the N = 1 case. List the option types that count as mild risk, and state that the ordinary 'when in doubt, risky' default applies in all other months.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk** (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately or off the record, anonymous moves, side deals, partial, phased or postponed fixes
weaknesses.problem: The skill relies on invented mechanics (an HR remark as a risk gauge, keyword-to-stat mappings, a review talk 'arriving' at fixed months, 'friendly/quiet/frowning' tones). It labels them 'working assumptions', but the decision rules then treat them as firm. The long keyword lists also behave like fixed answers for particular event wordings, and they weaken robustness when wording changes. Some of it is wrong. Challenging rules through a formal channel is presumed risky, and the review timing is guessed.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the keyword lists to a few general principles (open, honest and complete handling is safer than hidden or partial handling). Say that you should infer effects from the stat changes shown after each choice. Drop the claims about when the review talk arrives and about HR remark tones unless the game shows them. Keep only rules grounded in the handbook.

weaknesses.quote: Before choosing, read every option for the likely sign of its effect on Skill, Network, Output, Health, Dignity, Wealth and hidden risk. ... Then apply these steps in order. Skip a step if it would remove every option.
weaknesses.problem: The story logic is a dense five-step cascade with exceptions nested inside exceptions (N=1 versus N=2, Concerns counter, Stalled, Best, Expect). A flash-class model will struggle to apply it reliably on every turn. The status-line bookkeeping (Best, Stalled, Expect, Concerns) costs tokens and is easy to get wrong. Steps 2 and 4 conflict at N=1 and the exception only partly resolves it.
weaknesses.fix: Shrink the story procedure to 3-4 steps: avoid anything that could end the run, avoid risky or hidden options, fix low stats, then pick the option that most raises Skill, Network and Output. Reduce the status line to 'Review in N | S N O | Health Dignity Wealth'. Remove Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns, or make them optional.

weaknesses.quote: Health or Dignity in the lower part of its 0–10 range (our margin: 4 or below, not a published limit) or falling three months in a row; ... No Skill learning or High-intensity work until it recovers.
weaknesses.problem: Thresholds of 4 or below are broad and invented. The main-action table and the last-quarter rules are rigid. The 'Defuse legacy risk' rule is driven only by the HR remark tone and can burn 2 of 3 Energy every quarter. A stat at 5 gets no guidance, and the Skill/Output growth the promotion needs gets starved. There is also no plan for how much wealth to hold or for pacing across the early, middle and late game, beyond the final month.
weaknesses.fix: Give a simple graded rule: at Health or Dignity 3 or below, recover first. At 4-6, mix recovery with growth. At 7 or above, invest. Add phase goals, for example build Skill and Network in months 1-18, push promotions in the middle, and protect Health, Dignity and Wealth in the last year. Limit Defuse legacy risk to once or twice a year unless the warnings persist.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N:** N = 6 - (current_month mod 6), and N = 6 when current_month is a multiple of 6. ... The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: Invents mechanics that the published rules do not give: that the last month before a review is the decisive one, that the review talk arrives at specific months, and that month 47 is the last review month. These are unverified, and the handbook describes review as performance over a longer period. The rule 'the last review comes as month 48 starts' is also internally inconsistent with the N formula, which makes month 48 N = 6.
weaknesses.fix: Describe review timing as 'every 6 months' only, and say that sustained trends matter more than one month. Remove the claims about talk timing and the N=1 deadline, or mark them clearly as unverified. Make the month-47 and month-48 handling consistent.

weaknesses.quote: Review close (N = 1 or 2). ... With N = 1, apply all of this step. Drop options that may lower Skill, Network or Output ... A mild risk (handling something privately, partially or later) is then acceptable when it is the only way to keep Skill, Network and Output
weaknesses.problem: The strategy overweights a single pre-review month, which contradicts the rule that promotion rests on 'sustained results rather than a single month'. It also permits risk-taking that conflicts with the handbook's warnings about hidden risk. Long chains of conditional steps, the status line and the Stalled bookkeeping add heavy complexity for a flash-class model.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the special-case N=1 exception with a steady priority order: survive, then hidden risk, then wellbeing, then balanced growth in Skill, Network and Output. Drop the mild-risk exception.

weaknesses.quote: Start every note with: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The status line is long and its Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns tracking demands a lot of bookkeeping every turn. Errors in that bookkeeping would cascade, the token cost rises, and the agent's memory scheme relies on `check_latest_logs` recovering the notes. Many of the heuristics (Stalled inference, 'usually' stat effects) are unverified guesses.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to a short line such as month, the three key stats, Health, Dignity and the HR remark tone. Drop Best, Stalled and Concerns, and keep only the few story-option heuristics that are most reliable.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N:** N = 6 - (current_month mod 6), and N = 6 when current_month is a multiple of 6. ... The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: The review timing is inconsistent and partly invented. The handbook says the review happens every 6 months, and quarterly phases fall at months 3, 6 and so on. The skill instead claims month 47 is the last review month and the last review comes as month 48 starts. It also treats N = 6 as the review month while calling N = 1 the deadline. This is confusing, and it presents unpublished timing as fact.
weaknesses.fix: Say plainly that the review is at the end of months 6, 12, 18 and so on. Define 'months to review' as 6 minus (month mod 6). Mark any finer timing as an assumption, and drop the claim about month 47 and 48 unless it is verified.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, ... and challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: These are long keyword lists of assumed effects. They are not published rules, and some, such as the 'even through a formal channel' case, are strongly speculative. They push the agent toward fixed answers, which is close to the prohibited pattern. The skill also leans on an 'HR remark' that is not in the public rules. A wrong inference could hurt play.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the lists with a short principle: prefer open, documented, complete actions and avoid concealment. Keep the 'working assumptions' label. Drop the speculative items and the dependence on an unpublished HR remark, or say it is only used if it actually appears.

weaknesses.quote: Status line ... `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0` ... Stalled: a provisional record of an expected gain that did not show up
weaknesses.problem: The bookkeeping is heavy. It has a per-turn status line with Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns, plus a 5-step story ladder with an exception inside it and 6 quarterly rules. A flash-class model will likely get this wrong or skip it, and the 'Concerns' and 'Stalled' mechanics add little value. The skill also gives no overall plan for the 48 months, such as early skill and network building and a late-game wealth and health focus.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the status line to 'Review in N | S N O | Health Dignity Wealth'. Remove Best, Stalled and Concerns. Add a short phase plan, for example months 1–12 build Skill and Network, 13–40 balance toward promotion, and 41–48 protect Health, Dignity, Wealth and risk.

weaknesses.quote: then, with the Energy left, Health recovery and Mental recovery while either is below full, then Network maintenance
weaknesses.problem: Quarterly line 1 spends more than the 3 Energy budget. Defuse legacy risk costs 2, which leaves 1, so only one 1-cost action fits, yet the line lists three more actions in sequence.
weaknesses.fix: Make the order explicit and affordable: "Defuse legacy risk (2) if the HR remark is not friendly; then one 1-cost action: Health recovery if Health is below Dignity, otherwise Mental recovery if Dignity is below full."

weaknesses.quote: Remove a stat from Stalled only when your level changes or when Now is below the value written for it (it lost ground and can be raised again); a stat sitting at its written value stays in Stalled even if months pass.
weaknesses.problem: The Stalled bookkeeping has several interacting conditions (Expect values, one-quarter check, reset rules, the 'stays even if months pass' exception). A model reading this in a long run is likely to misapply it, so the Energy and main-action choices become unpredictable.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce it to one rule: "A stat enters Stalled when a quarterly action or story choice meant to raise it does not raise it at the next observe. It leaves Stalled only when your level changes." Drop the Expect field.

weaknesses.quote: in our development runs the stat that took longest to raise from level 4 on was Skill, while Network and Output stopped showing gains early in each level
weaknesses.problem: This is an unpublished empirical claim presented as the basis for the level-4+ plan. The game rules do not support it, and the agent cannot verify it, so it reads as an invented mechanic.
weaknesses.fix: Remove the claim. State the plan as a decision rule based on what observe shows, for example: "From level 4, if Skill has not risen over the last two quarterly phases, prioritise Skill learning."

weaknesses.quote: in our development runs the stat that took longest to raise from level 4 on was Skill, while Network and Output stopped showing gains early in each level
weaknesses.problem: Unverifiable empirical claim presented as the basis for a rule. The published rules say nothing about which stat is slowest, so the agent is told to prioritise Skill from level 4 on with no in-game support.
weaknesses.fix: Delete the claim. State the priority as a conditional on what observe shows: if Skill's gain is slower than Network's or Output's over the last two reviews, weight Skill.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: Invented mechanic. The handbook says only that a formal review happens every six months. It does not say when the review talk arrives or that later choices stop counting. The N = 1 deadline logic depends on this.
weaknesses.fix: Write: 'Formal reviews come every six months (handbook). Treat the month before each review (N = 1) as the highest-stakes month for Skill, Network and Output, without claiming that later choices have no effect.'

weaknesses.quote: in our runs a career with Dignity kept high met fewer blow-ups
weaknesses.problem: Fabricated supporting evidence used to justify a wellbeing threshold (margin 7). It presents an assumption as an observed result and makes the agent over-weight Dignity.
weaknesses.fix: Keep the published basis only: 'Dignity is a published failure direction; keep it away from the bottom of its range.' Mark the 7 threshold explicitly as a judgement call, not as a finding.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count, and a single lost point there can cost the promotion.
weaknesses.problem: Presents an unpublished timing rule for the review talk and a 'last month whose choices count' window as fact. The handbook only says reviews happen every six months, so this is an invented mechanic that drives the N = 1 exception in step 2.
weaknesses.fix: State only the published cadence: 'Reviews happen every six months (months 6, 12, 18 …). Treat the month before each review as a priority month; the exact evaluation window is not published.'

weaknesses.quote: in our development runs the stat that took longest to raise from level 4 on was Skill, while Network and Output stopped showing gains early in each level.
weaknesses.problem: An unverifiable empirical claim that is used to justify the level-4+ Skill focus (quarterly line 5 and the double-counted Skill gain in step 5). The agent cannot check it in a run and it is not a published rule.
weaknesses.fix: Remove the development-run claim. Justify the Skill emphasis from published facts (promotion considers Skill, Network and Output; Skill learning is a published Energy action) and let the agent adjust from observed Now and Best values.

weaknesses.quote: a stat sitting at its written value stays in Stalled even if months pass.
weaknesses.problem: Combined with 'Remove a stat from Stalled only when your level changes or when Now is below the value written for it', a stat can be blocked for the rest of a level with no time limit. The bookkeeping is also fragile after summaries, so the agent may drop or misread the status line and the rule stops applying.
weaknesses.fix: Replace with one simple rule: clear every Stalled entry at each six-month review and after any level change, and cap a stalled stat's skip to one review window.

weaknesses.quote: Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0
weaknesses.problem: The status-line bookkeeping (Best, Stalled, Expect, Concerns) is very complex and has many interacting rules. A flash-class model will likely get it wrong or drift, and it eats tokens on every turn. Stalled also rests on an unpublished assumption that stats stop rising, and it can suppress useful investment.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the note to a short line such as 'Review in N | S/N/O | HR remark'. Drop Best, Stalled, Expect and Concerns, or keep only one simple trend check.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: This states invented timing and mechanics as fact. The handbook says the review happens at months 6, 12 and so on, and the Skill also claims 'The last review comes as month 48 starts'. The 'last month whose choices count' claim is also unverified. The Skill also gives hard numeric margins (Health 4, Dignity 7, Health above 6) and an unpublished 'HR remark' classification, which are only partly flagged as assumptions.
weaknesses.fix: Say only that reviews come every 6 months and promotion uses Skill, Network and Output. Mark every timing claim and margin as a heuristic, and remove the claim about which month counts.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately or off the record, anonymous moves, side deals, partial, phased or postponed fixes
weaknesses.problem: This is a long keyword-matching list of assumed effects. It is dense and could be read as a lookup table of fixed answers. The Dignity margin (keep it at 7 or above) makes the story rules over-restrictive. Step 2 and Step 4 conflict through the 'Exception for N = 1' and are hard to apply.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce it to a few principles (be transparent, own mistakes, fix problems fully, avoid shortcuts). Merge the review-close rules into one short priority order and remove the N = 1 exception.

weaknesses.quote: Read every option for the likely sign of its effect on Skill, Network, Output, Health, Dignity, Wealth and hidden risk. ... Then apply these steps in order. Skip a step if it would remove every option.
weaknesses.problem: The skill is long and dense: it has nested exceptions, a Stalled/Best/Expect bookkeeping scheme, and cross-references between sections. A flash-class model will likely misapply or drop parts of it. That undermines the clarity and executability the rubric rewards.
weaknesses.fix: Cut it to about half the length. Remove the Stalled/Expect machinery and the double counting. Keep a short priority ladder: survive, then risk, then wellbeing, then review prep, then growth. Add one compact status-line format.

weaknesses.quote: The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: The review timing is asserted as fact and is inconsistent. The handbook only says a review happens every 6 months. The skill also says 'The last review comes as month 48 starts', which conflicts with N = 6 - (month mod 6). The invented timing and the 'lost point costs the promotion' claim mislead the agent about when to prepare.
weaknesses.fix: Say only that reviews happen every 6 months. Tell the agent to read the observed month and events for review timing, and to raise Skill, Network and Output steadily in the 2 months before each review. Remove the claims about the month-47 and month-48 review order.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky. ... Output rises when you deliver, ship, finish...
weaknesses.problem: Many stat-effect heuristics (Output falls when helping others, hidden risk rises with 'challenging the company' formally) are presented as likely mechanics. They are only partly flagged as assumptions, and 'in our development runs' claims the agent cannot verify. Over-avoiding risk can also stop the agent from growing.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the heuristics to a few that the visible game feedback supports. Label them once as hints, with the option text and the observed stat changes taking precedence. Drop the unverifiable claims about development runs and tune the risk wording to be less absolute.

weaknesses.quote: Lines below that say how options "usually" move a stat are our working assumptions for reading option text, not game rules.
weaknesses.problem: Much of the Skill is built on invented mechanics, such as Skill rising when you analyse and Output falling when you help others. It also states the review timing as fact: "The review talk arrives as a new six-month block starts" and "The last review comes as month 48 starts". These are not in the published rules. The caveat helps, but the agent still treats the mechanics as decision rules. This risks mismatches with the game and with the 'invented mechanics presented as rules' criterion.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the speculative stat-effect heuristics down to a few short, clearly labelled hints. Base decisions on the effects the game actually displays after each choice. Remove or soften the claims about exactly when reviews and review talks occur.

weaknesses.quote: `Review in N | Now S<Skill> N<Network> O<Output> | Best S<..> N<..> O<..> | Stalled: none | Concerns this month: 0`
weaknesses.problem: The status-line bookkeeping is heavy: Best, Stalled and Expect, plus a provisional Stalled rule with its own removal conditions. It is hard for a flash-class model to follow reliably and it eats note budget. The wording is also self-referential and dense, for example the Stalled definition and the 'counting twice' scoring. The 5-step story procedure also has exceptions nested inside it, which makes it ambiguous.
weaknesses.fix: Simplify the note to 'Review in N | S/N/O | Health/Dignity/Wealth | HR remark'. Drop Best/Stalled/Expect and Concerns. Reduce the story procedure to a short ordered priority list with one exception at most.

weaknesses.quote: Dignity is not near the top of its range (our margin: 7 or below), drop options that lower it
weaknesses.problem: The thresholds are arbitrary and over-conservative. Dignity at 7 or below counts as a limit, which would apply almost always and dominate the choice. The Skill also biases the whole career toward defensive play, because it drops any possibly risky option. Wealth and the ending score, which depend on level and growth, get little explicit weight across the 48 months. There is no phase-based plan for months 1–12, 13–36 and 37–48.
weaknesses.fix: Set the low-stat triggers to published danger zones, such as Health or Dignity at 3 or below, and use a softer preference for values above that. Add a simple three-phase 48-month plan with the ending dimensions (level, wealth, skill, network, risk control) as explicit targets.
